chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Isa ibn Ayoub from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Al-Fadl ibn Yunus from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: 'Frequently say: O Allah, do not make me among those who borrow (the religion temporarily), and do not remove me from deficiency.'
I said, 'As for the temporary ones, I know that a man borrows the religion then exits from it. So what is the meaning of "do not remove me from deficiency"?'

He said: 'For every deed you do for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, be deficient in your own estimation, for all people are deficient in their deeds between themselves and Allah, except for whom Allah preserves.'

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرِ: Deficiency or shortcoming; here referring to a spiritual state of humility where one considers their own deeds insufficient.
key_terms.الْمُعَارِينَ: Those who borrow (temporarily); people who temporarily adopt the religion or faith and then abandon it.
key_terms.عَصَمَهُ: He preserved/protected him; referring to divine preservation from major deficiency or error.
key_terms.مُقَصِّرًا: Deficient; one who considers their actions lacking in perfection.

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of being 'deficient' (muqassir) in Shia Islamic spirituality and how does it differ from negligence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that 'deficiency' (taqsir) is not a spiritual failing but a virtuous state of humble self-awareness, where the believer constantly perceives their own deeds as insufficient before Allah. This concept underscores the Shia emphasis on continuous self-reflection and the prevention of spiritual arrogance, distinguishing between the deficiency of action and the deficiency of perception. By maintaining this mindset, the believer avoids the trap of complacency, ensuring that their worship remains sincere and enduring.
